extracted.intended_audience: The New Yorker readers and contest entrants (anyone age 13+)
extracted.subtask_description: Participate in The New Yorker weekly Cartoon Caption Contest by submitting a humorous caption for the provided cartoon; editors pick three finalists and readers vote on the winner. The page describes the contest workflow, eligibility, timelines, and shows past finalists/winner examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly format and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Each week, we provide a cartoon in need of a caption. You, the reader, submit your caption below, we choose three finalists, and you vote for your favorite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the recurring cadence and end-to-end process: weekly cartoon prompt → reader submissions → editors select three finalists → public voting determines the winner. Finalists for a given week's cartoon are published online on a stated date and also appear in a forthcoming print issue (example: finalists will appear online June 25th and in the July 2nd, 2018 issue).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader submission
rubrics_metrics.description: You, the reader, submit your caption below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are made online on the contest page. The page encourages active participation (submit a caption for the current week's cartoon). Examples of successful captions are shown on the site (past winners and placings) but the page does not list technical submission limits or formatting rules (those are in the full rules link).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of three finalists
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors/selectors (the site) select three finalist captions from the pool of submissions. The page notes that three finalists will be presented for public voting and that those finalists will be published online and in the magazine on specified dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public voting to pick the winner
rubrics_metrics.description: You vote for your favorite caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After finalists are posted, site visitors/readers cast votes to pick the week's winner. The page also invites readers to help pick finalists from the previous week by rating submissions ('Help us pick three finalists from last week’s contest by rating submissions. Vote now »').

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — age requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone age thirteen or older can enter or vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly states the minimum age for entry and voting; additional eligibility, prize, and entry details are referenced in the complete rules (linked).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete official rules available
rubrics_metrics.description: To read the complete rules, click here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page points to a separate full-rules document for detailed terms, conditions, entry requirements, copyright/usage, and other procedural details not shown on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and examples of winners/finalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners and finalists are announced and examples are shown (e.g., winner: 'His words, not mine.' — Jack Buchignani, Los Angeles, Calif.; second place: 'I'm the new micromanager.' — Sienna Jones, Emmaus, Pa.; third place: 'We demand time and a half.' — Lonewolf Williams, Lakewood, Colo.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page demonstrates the kinds of captions that have succeeded (brief, punchy lines often with a twist). These published examples serve as informal guidance on tone and length, though they are illustrative rather than prescriptive.
